steps.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: single full-frame portrait photorealistic interior mockup.
Input image 1 (IMG_8638) is the EDIT TARGET and locks this view from the hall doorway towards fireplace and bay. Input image 2 (IMG_8650) is a SUPPORTING reference for the same room's furniture, piano, shelves and actual geometry, NOT a second panel.
Preserve image 1's camera, black steel door framing and narrow room proportions. Show a single finished photograph, not before/after or collage. Piano can remain naturally partly obscured by original glazed door as in source, do not move architecture to show it.
Design proposal: "Reception Room 01 - A Considered Study". This is the same room and SAME design in both supplied photographs.
Existing room must remain exact: taupe/greige walls, white picture-frame mouldings, original white ceiling relief panels/cornice/rose and crystal chandelier, bay sash windows and white café sheers, white mantel/fireplace and black hearth, built-in alcove shelves/base cupboards with their same shelf number, positions, joinery and paint, original light oak plank floor, black steel glazed doors. No painting, construction, new openings, wall panels or enlarged room.
KEEP BOTH ORIGINAL GREEN VELVET ARMCHAIRS, their bentwood arms, their silhouettes/colour and actual size, original black upright piano and bench on hall-side right wall, original oak-top black-frame sit-stand desk with TWO black monitors in bay, original black office task chair. Do NOT replace these with generic furniture or hide working equipment to make a prettier room.
SAME PHYSICAL ARRANGEMENT IN BOTH VIEWS:
- Reception/reading zone at left, beside fireplace: retain one green chair on each side of the hearth as in original but pull them slightly into room and angle each gently inward, forming a loose conversational pair. Modest movement only, not placing chair across piano or desk route. Both faces and actual bentwood arms recognisable.
- A large rectangular low-pile wool rug anchors ONLY this left seating zone. Roughly 180x240 to 200x250 cm as a proportional concept, length along the fireplace wall. Soft warm stone / mushroom-tobacco brown with a faint aged Persian/floral drawing in adjacent brown shades, little muted moss and dusty rust, matte, sophisticated LOW-CONTRAST pattern with a similarly faded border. No bright orange, bold geometric motifs, crisp black perimeter, plain sisal or fake shiny rug. Front feet of both green chairs sit on rug. Do not carpet the whole floor. Visible oak route along right between piano and seating, unobstructed approach to bay workstation. Desk chair roll space remains on oak, not catching the rug edge.
- Remove floating oak wheeled pedestal from middle: reposition it neatly at outer edge of bay desk if possible WITHOUT crowding user's knees or sit-stand mechanism; if not feasible, move it out of this room as a proposed relocation, don't pretend to shrink it. Remove bags/loose clothing/paper mess. Do not remove piano or workstation.
- Small round dark walnut pedestal occasional/coffee table, approx 50-55cm diameter and 45-48cm high, between chairs but shifted away from centre of walking route and clear of hearth. Table carries exactly ONE small simple ceramic coaster/dish, nothing else. No large sofa, extra armchair, bench or bulky footstool.
- Each chair has ONE restrained cushion: nearer chair warm oatmeal linen with subtle fine brown woven stripe; farther/bay-side chair muted dusty-rust linen. No blanket piles.
SHELF STYLING: Recompose existing books and a small selection of objects, preserve actual shelf architecture. Elegant considered BOOKSHELVES not a shop of ornaments. Place purposeful groups of varied book sizes, real-looking clothbound and ordinary books in muted browns, greens, cream and burgundy (not uniform fake book sets or rainbow), mostly upright with an occasional low horizontal stack; leave generous empty gaps. Across both alcoves at most 2-3 modest personal picture frames, one olive ceramic vessel and one aged earthenware bowl, in asymmetrical balanced groups. A few meaningful objects only, not an ornament in every gap. No huge plants or trailing vines hiding books, no new shelves, no fake text. Books not packed in every inch, use around half to two-thirds of available shelf space. Conceal small loose miscellaneous items in existing lower cupboards. Style shelves consistently in both views.
FIREPLACE: retain existing wide framed architectural print above mantel. Remove row of three small plant pots from mantel (reuse elsewhere in home); mantel has ONE modest olive ceramic vase at one end and ONE small unlit aged-brass candlestick at the other, with clear centre. Keep black hearth visible and empty/clear for actual use, move wicker hearth basket to a practical cupboard/storage location rather than pretending fireplace is seating. Do not ignite fire or put rug/table across hearth.
LIGHTING / WINDOW: replace existing white uplighter with one slender aged-brass reading floor lamp with small warm oatmeal linen shade, located behind bay-side green armchair near alcove, out of desk/circulation route. No lamp on piano. Small understated aged-brass adjustable desk task lamp at desk side if it fits, respect monitor space. Retain sheer/café curtains and trial soft full-length warm-flax linen outer panels stacked back only at outer bay ends, no blocking window light, same window geometry and existing curtain provision (hardware capacity to be verified, not new architecture). No new ceiling fixture or wall sconces.
PIANO / STUDY: preserve piano/bench, lid, keyboard and physical form, piano top with at most one small meaningful framed landscape and tidy music, no plants or water vessels on piano. Keep BOTH monitors and original office chair. Tidy cables under/behind desk into a discreet tray, no free-hanging cable mass, no imaginary disappearing workstation. Existing small floor plant by piano can be retained tucked at bay edge in a modest pot if it fits, not filling pathway.
Palette: actual unchanged greige walls, existing green velvet, warm oak, subdued brown/stone wool, dark walnut, tiny dusty-rust touches and aged brass. Curated, elegant and chic, natural real home, no accessory clutter. Realistic daylight with small warm reading light, paint colours remain accurate. Photorealistic interior photography, actual materials and proportions, no text/labels/watermarks, no illustrated or glossy CGI style.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is EDIT TARGET, portrait doorway view. Input image 2 is SUPPORTING reference, a wider view of the SAME proposed room. Make only a few small adjustments to image 1 to align desk and mantel styling with image 2. Do not copy image 2 camera or crop.
1. The oak mobile drawer pedestal should be at the RIGHT END of bay desk when facing the window, towards piano, exactly as reference image 2. Remove the pedestal currently at LEFT of desk in image 1 and restore oak floor/wall behind it accurately. Put that same original-size pedestal to right of desk, where it may be mostly hidden by foreground steel door or office chair. Do not move desk, shrink drawers or block chair knee/roll space. Prefer natural occlusion to moving door/room.
2. The small brass adjustable desk task lamp belongs on RIGHT END of desk as in reference2, not left. Move only that lamp, keep TWO monitors and task chair unchanged.
3. Mantel vase: retain olive vase at left with just a few short fine airy foliage sprigs as reference2, no bouquet or large branches. Brass candlestick at right stays.
Preserve portrait camera, original taupe and white paint, exact ceiling relief/cornice/chandelier, sash bay/sheers/linen outer panels, shelves and cabinets, both original green bentwood chairs/cushions, reading floor lamp, black upright piano and bench, small walnut round table, current subdued brown patterned rug and exposed oak walking route. Do not alter shelves, rug, paintings, wall architecture, lighting or furniture design. No people/text/watermarks. One portrait photorealistic image; maintain detailed photographic materials.
